title: One of the Svalbard cables goes down and stays unexplained
description: Infrastructure damage with a culprit that is never established. One of the two subsea fibre cables to the archipelago fails; the survey finds physical damage consistent with a dragged anchor and cannot establish intent; a vessel was in the area and its track is incomplete. Correct end state: hostile probability moderate and stable, attribution unresolved, and no irreversible action taken on an unresolved infrastructure incident.

injects.content: Loss of continuity on one of the two Svalbard fibre pairs. Fault located by reflectometry at approximately 130 km from the mainland landing, in water depth consistent with fishing and transit activity. The second cable is carrying all traffic and is now a single point of failure for the archipelago.

Downlink data from the Svalbard site now constrained by the surviving cable. Prioritisation required: we cannot move all customers' data. If the second pair fails, the site's product goes to store-and-forward and every user's picture degrades by hours.

A cargo vessel transited the fault area within the estimated window. Its transponder shows a gap of about four hours across that period. Transponder gaps in this area are common and usually mundane; the vessel's flag, ownership and charterer are in three different jurisdictions, which is also common.

Physical damage observed at the fault location: the cable has been displaced roughly 200 metres from its charted position and shows external abrasion consistent with a dragged anchor or heavy trawl gear. The damage is consistent with an anchor drag. It is equally consistent with a deliberate anchor drag. The survey cannot distinguish the two and no survey can.

Statement expresses concern at reports of damage to civilian communications infrastructure serving the archipelago, notes that the archipelago's inhabitants include a Russian community with treaty-protected rights, and asks whether Norwegian administration of the cables meets its obligations to all users.
Repair vessel mobilised. Weather-dependent, earliest on-station in nine days, splice and test three days after that. Until then the archipelago runs on one pair.
